stem: The sample space is the whole numbers from 1 to 15, drawn as the rectangle. Event $A$ and event $B$ are the two overlapping circles. Shade the region that holds every outcome of $A\cap B$.
solution: Read the symbol $A\cap B$ as "$A$ and $B$": an outcome belongs to it only if it is in $A$ and also in $B$ at the same time.
The only part of the diagram that lies inside both circles is the overlap, so shade just that.
Do not shade the part of $A$ outside the overlap or the part of $B$ outside the overlap: each of those outcomes is in one event only.
Leave the part of the rectangle outside both circles unshaded too: those outcomes are in neither event.
notes: Genuine fit: the student picks out the one region inside both circles, which is what "only the elements that are in both sets" means. The widget's shade/intersection case can emit only off-target, so this template has one diagnostic and it is a judgement call. off-target is mapped to either-set-not-both because the stem names both events and the and/or confusion (shading everything inside either circle, the union) is the likeliest wrong shading by a wide margin. It also fires for whole-set-not-intersection (shading one whole circle, overlap included), which the student would wrongly be told is a both-circles error. Samuel may prefer to drop this diagnostic and ship the question with a plain "not quite" until venn_builder can name those two shadings apart (see top-level notes). No figure is referenced: the instrument is the diagram.
